q-174435:
The union of a family of indexed sets is the set containing all elements belonging to *at least one* set in the indexed family:

$$
{⋃}_{i\in I}{A}_{i}={x\in U\,:\,x\in {A}_{i}\,\,\text{for at least one }{A}_{i},\,\,i\in I}
$$

where $U$ is a universal set.

Therefore, in our case, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{⋃}_{i\in I}{S}_{i} & ={S}_{5}\cup {S}_{6}\cup {S}_{7} \\  & =[5,6)\,\cup \,[6,7)\,\cup \,[7,8) \\  & =[5,8).\end{aligned}
$$

q-174450:
The union of a family of indexed sets is the set containing all elements belonging to *at least one* set in the indexed family:

$$
{⋃}_{i\in I}{A}_{i}={x\in U\,:\,x\in {A}_{i}\,\,\text{for at least one }{A}_{i},\,\,i\in I}
$$

where $U$ is a universal set.

Let's now write down a few instances of our indexed sets:

- if $i=1,$ we have ${X}_{1}={-1,0,1}$

- if $i=2,$ we have ${X}_{2}={-2,0,2}$

- if $i=3,$ we have ${X}_{3}={-3,0,3}$

and so on. 

Notice that all the integers belong to one of the sets.

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{⋃}_{i\in I}{X}_{i}=Z.\end{aligned}
$$

q-174447:
The intersection of a family of indexed sets ${{A}_{i}}_{i\in I}$ contains all elements that belong to *all* sets in our family:

$$
{⋂}_{i\in I}{A}_{i}={x\in U\,:\,x\in {A}_{i}\,\,\text{for all }{A}_{i},\,\,i\in I}
$$

where $U$ is a universal set.

Let's now write down a few instances of our indexed sets:

- if $i=-1,$ we have ${X}_{-1}={-2,-1}$

- if $i=0,$ we have ${X}_{0}={-1,0}$

- if $i=1,$ we have ${X}_{1}={0,1}$

and so on. 

Notice that there is no element that belongs to all the sets. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{⋂}_{i\in I}{X}_{i}=∅.\end{aligned}
$$

q-91159:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries above and below ${a}_{21}=-1$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-7 & 4 & 3 \\ -1 & 2 & 2 \\ -8 & 6 & 4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-7{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & -10 & -11 \\ -1 & 2 & 2 \\ -8 & 6 & 4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-8{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & -10 & -11 \\ -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -10 & -12\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-7{R}_{2}\,$ and $\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-8{R}_{2}.$

q-130448:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make the entries below ${a}_{12}=-2$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 3 \\ -5 & 8 & -7 \\ -3 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 3 \\ 11 & 0 & 5 \\ -3 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 3 \\ 11 & 0 & 5 \\ 1 & 0 & 7\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1}\,$ and $\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}.$

q-42917:

To do this, we can apply the following elementary column operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 3 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-3{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-7 & 2 & 2 \\ -2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-4{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-7 & -6 & 2 \\ -2 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}

q-91189:

$$

$$

q-42562:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 8 & 6 & -2 \\ 1 & 4 & 5 & -3 \\ -2 & -5 & -3 & 8 \\ -1 & -1 & -4 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}-4{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 6 & -2 \\ 1 & 0 & 5 & -3 \\ -2 & 3 & -3 & 8 \\ -1 & 3 & -4 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-5{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -4 & -2 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & -3 \\ -2 & 3 & 7 & 8 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+3{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -4 & 4 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 3 & 7 & 2 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding elementary column operations are

\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 8 & 0 & 4 \\ 6 & 9 & 1 & 3 \\ -6 & -1 & 1 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-2{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ -16 & 8 & 0 & 4 \\ -12 & 9 & 1 & 3 \\ -4 & -1 & 1 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-2{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ -16 & 8 & -16 & 4 \\ -12 & 9 & -17 & 3 \\ -4 & -1 & 3 & -6\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{4}:={C}_{4}-3{C}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ -16 & 8 & -16 & -20 \\ -12 & 9 & -17 & -24 \\ -4 & -1 & 3 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =B.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding elementary column operations are

$\,$ ${C}_{1}:={C}_{1}-2{C}_{2}\,$ and $\,{C}_{3}:={C}_{3}-2{C}_{2}.$

q-1226:
The set $C∖D$ is the set of all elements belonging to $C$ but *not* $D.$ Note that the elements $-1,0\in D$ are also in $C,$ so we must remove them. Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}C∖D & =C-D \\  & ={-3,-1,0,5,10}-{-2,-1,0,1} \\  & ={-3,5,10}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-1225:
The set $Y-X$ is the set of all elements belonging to $Y$ but *not* $X.$ Note that the elements $1,3\in X$ are also in $Y,$ so we must remove them. Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Y-X & ={1,2,3,4}-{1,3,5,7} \\  & ={2,4}.\end{aligned}
$$

q-81766:
The multiples of $3$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
A={3,6,9,12,15,18,21,24,…}.
$$

Likewise, multiples of $4$ that are greater than $0$ are

$$
B={4,8,12,16,20,24,…}.
$$

Now, $B-A$ is the *difference* of $B$ and $A,$ which means that we want to find the elements that are in $B$ but *not* in $A.$

The elements of $B$ that are also in $A$ are $12,24,$ and so on (i.e. multiples of $12$). So, we must remove these elements from $B.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}B-A & ={4,8,12,16,20,24,…}-{3,6,9,12,15,18,21,24,…} \\  & ={4,8,16,20,…}.\end{aligned}
$$
